description.value: The study tested whether apathetic and disinhibited behavioral presentations of the frontal variant of frontotemporal lobar degeneration are associated with distinct patterns of cerebral glucose hypometabolism and measured cerebral 5-HT2A receptor density in a subset of patients using PET.

spans.text: This study had two primary goals: (1) to test the hypothesis that different behavioral aspects in fv-FTLD are caused by degeneration of selective frontal areas, which is reflected in different patterns of brain glucose hypometabolism; and (2) to measure cerebral 5-HT2A receptor densities in the same patients in the early phase of the disease, using PET and [11C]MDL100,907, because no in vivo data about this receptor subtype are available in the fv-FTLD.

design.value: A comparative PET study of 18 patients with the frontal variant of frontotemporal lobar degeneration, classified into apathetic and disinhibited behavioral groups, and healthy control subjects; eight patients and six healthy volunteers additionally underwent [11C]MDL100,907 PET for 5-HT2A receptor binding.

spans.text: We studied cerebral glucose uptake using (18)F-fluorodeoxyglucose and positron emission tomography in 18 patients fulfilling clinical criteria for fv-FTLD and showing, respectively, an apathetic or disinhibited behavioral syndrome. In eight of these patients, we also evaluated the 5-hydroxytryptamine-2A receptor cerebral receptor distribution with [(11)C]MDL and positron emission tomography.

name.value: comparison between eight patients in the FTLD group and six healthy control subjects

spans.text: We used Statistical Parametric Mapping 2 (SPM2) procedures to assess differences of the distribution density of 5-HT2A receptors in a comparison between eight patients in the FTLD group and six healthy control subjects.

In the eight patients in the FTLD group, the binding of the tracer to 5-HT2A receptors, compared with healthy control subjects, was significantly reduced bilaterally in the ventromedial frontopolar cortex (left: -2, 58, 4; Z-score, 3.1; voxel extent, 128; right: 6, 54, 4; Z-score, 3.8; voxel extent, 128), frontal medial cortex (2, 58, 12; Z-score, 3.2; voxel extent, 128), anterior cingulate cortex (left/right: 2, 28, 32; Z-score, 3.2; voxel extent, 6), and the midbrain (left/right: 2, -14, -4; Z-score, 3.8; voxel extent, 35).
The left dorsolateral frontal cortex (left: -26, 24, 52; Z-score, 3.5, voxel extent, 15) was also hypometabolic (p < 0.001; Fig 3).
